contributions.headingText: Oncocytic sinonasal papilloma (OSP) is a benign epithelial neoplasm of ectodermally derived sinonasal epithelium showing multilayered oncocytic cuboidal to columnar epithelium.
2F00.Y & XH17Q9 Other specified benign neoplasm of middle ear or respiratory system & Papilloma, NOS
Not recommended: oncocytic Schneiderian papilloma; cylindrical cell papilloma; columnar cell papilloma; Ringertz papilloma.

OSP involves the lateral wall of the nasal cavity and/or paranasal sinuses (most commonly the maxillary sinus) and may also rarely involve other head and neck sites, including the middle ear {4323842; 6370825; 8615588; 23595801; 31890872; 34021464}.

Patients with OSP typically present with unilateral nasal obstruction and may also manifest rhinorrhoea, epistaxis, and/or anosmia {6370825; 23595801}.

Imaging

Imaging studies document a mass centred around the middle meatus, often with bone remodelling {23595801; 28861190; 29987980}. OSP appears similar to inverted sinonasal papilloma (ISP) on imaging, but studies have shown three distinctive features that may be helpful: T1-weighted high signal, multiple mucinous cystic foci, and a lack of focal osteitis {29987980}.

OSPs constitute 3–19% of all sinonasal papillomas {4323842; 8238761; 23595801}, estimated to have an incidence of 0.05 cases per 100 000 person-years {7837917}. They typically occur in older adults (peak incidence in the sixth to seventh decades of life), are rare in patients aged < 30 years, and have an equal sex distribution {23595801; 31890872}.
There are no confirmed risk factors. HPV infection is not an etiological factor {7837916; 29145573}.

Oncogenic hotspot mutations in KRAS exon 2 or 3 stimulate tumour growth via constitutive KRAS activity and downstream activation of the MAPK and PI3K/AKT pathways {17428555; 32203683}. Malignant progression of OSP to sinonasal carcinoma is associated with deleterious TP53 and CDKN2A mutations {33203919}.
OSP has a papillary and/or polypoid gross appearance; tumours can be very large (> 100 mm) but are typically < 50 mm {6370825}.

OSP is a non-invasive papillary epithelial neoplasm with mixed exophytic and endophytic growth {4323842; 6370825}. Tumours comprise multiple layers of cuboidal to columnar cells with abundant oncocytic cytoplasm, slightly enlarged and irregular but centrally placed nuclei, and small nucleoli. Scattered admixed ciliated or mucous columnar cells may be present superficially. Intraepithelial neutrophilic inflammation is common, whereas microcysts with mucin and/or neutrophilic microabscesses are characteristic. Epithelial dysplasia is uncommon in OSP but may manifest as increased nuclear atypia and/or mitotic activity {8238761; 2321700; 34021464}.
Essential: mixed exophytic and endophytic growth pattern; oncocytic cells with cuboidal to columnar morphology; intraepithelial microcysts with mucin and/or neutrophilic microabscesses.

Reported recurrence rates vary widely – from 6% to 40% of tumours in large studies with long-term follow-up – and these observed differences are probably multifactorial in origin, including tumour anatomical location (higher for paranasal sinus tumours) and surgical approach (higher with non-endoscopic techniques) {23595801; 31890872}.

Malignant transformation – either synchronous or metachronous – occurs in 3–17% of OSPs {8238761; 12172247; 23595801}; the vast majority of these tumours are keratinizing or non-keratinizing squamous cell carcinomas, but other types of malignancies have been reported (rarely), including adenocarcinoma, small cell carcinoma, and sinonasal undifferentiated carcinoma {11570918; 29879069}. OSP-associated mucoepidermoid carcinomas have been reported {8238761}; however, according to contemporary criteria, they most likely represent adenosquamous carcinomas.
